prompt:
Scene:
Same gothic nave as the reference, same single-point perspective, same camera height and lens. Cold blue advent procession: a long column of pilgrim silhouettes moves down the aisle toward the apse, with a deep teal mist replacing the warm haze.

Subject:
The identical rib-vaulted nave with the identical rose-window hologram, but the rose is now a slow rotating azure diagram of a compass-star pattern. A deep procession of hooded pilgrims carries tall cool-light staffs; the staffs emit narrow vertical cyan rays that punch upward through the AR scripture ribbons above, splitting them into short segments. Breath fog is visible near the floor.

Important details:
Keep the exact column spacing, rib-vault cadence, rose window location and symmetry from the reference. The light source has rotated: the ambient glow is now cold cyan from staffs and rose; the only warm spots are tiny amber halos trailing behind each pilgrim. Scripture ribbons must react visibly to the staff beams — bending, scattering, fragmenting around the rays. Pilgrim silhouettes stay simplified, no facial detail.

Use case:
Hologram Cathedral Nave series image 3/4, depends on the reference nave; demonstrates the same architecture during a cold advent procession.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no visible faces, no modern flashlights, no flags, no crosses carried as props, no commercial torch designs, keep the same nave identity as the reference.
